What to remember

A useful pilot connects graph fit, identity, relationships, evidence, mappings, validation, context, access, agent controls, ownership, and measures around one decision. The system may organize, retrieve, infer, validate, or draft. A named human remains accountable for the utility decision.

Module 18 completion

Complete every required item.

Questions learners ask

Clear up the remaining boundaries

Is Graph Fit Test the same as pilot?

No. In this lesson, Graph Fit Test and pilot perform different jobs. A useful pilot connects graph fit, identity, relationships, evidence, mappings, validation, context, access, agent controls, ownership, and measures around one decision.

What happens when operational question is missing?

The utility loses a named control in the path. In the module scenario, that makes the answer harder to trace, test, or approve.

Who owns competency?

A named utility role must own the definition or decision. A platform may execute the rule, but it does not become accountable.

Does this replace our existing utility systems?

No. Source systems keep doing their operating jobs. This lesson adds explicit meaning, evidence, and control across them.

When should we use a simpler approach?

Use the simplest governed design that answers the bounded question. If one reliable table is enough, do not add a graph only because graphs are available.

Sources and limits

Evidence boundary

This module uses an instructional utility scenario. It does not establish an operating procedure, legal conclusion, cybersecurity approval, or authority to act. Independent factual and practitioner review remain required.
